title: Neanderthal and early Homo sapiens behavior without species ranking
principle: Compare source-bounded behavioral constructs. Never convert the matrix into a scalar species score, cognitive ranking, or evolutionary ladder.

rows.interpretation: Both dossiers support intentional or structured mortuary behavior in particular contexts. Neither supports uniform species-wide practice or a specific theology.

left.title: Some Neanderthal groups intentionally buried some dead
left.evidence_balance: Modern in-situ and multidisciplinary site evidence supports intentional burial in particular cases. This does not imply uniform Neanderthal mortuary practice or a specific funerary theology.

right.title: Early Homo sapiens practiced structured mortuary behavior
right.evidence_balance: Qafzeh supports structured mortuary behavior in a specific early Homo sapiens context, but motive and cosmological interpretation remain underdetermined.

rows.construct: Deliberate display / abstract / graphic material behavior
rows.interpretation: Both sides contain deliberate material patterning or display behavior, but shells, pigments, engravings and graphic designs are not interchangeable traits and need artifact-level analysis.

left.title: Some Neanderthal populations produced abstract or symbolically used material culture
left.evidence_balance: The strongest observations establish deliberate material modification, pigment/ornament contexts and non-utilitarian structured marks. ‘Symbolic’ is a higher-level interpretation and must remain distinguishable from the physical observations.

right.title: Socially transmitted graphic and ornamental traditions existed in early Homo sapiens before 70 ka
right.evidence_balance: Independent material classes and regions support an early mosaic of display and graphic traditions, while the exact semantic content of those traditions remains partly underdetermined.

rows.construct: Does burial establish religion or afterlife doctrine?
rows.interpretation: The same inferential boundary applies on both sides: mortuary evidence can support purposeful treatment of the dead while leaving cosmology underdetermined.

left.title: Intentional burial proves formal religion or afterlife doctrine
left.evidence_balance: The current evidence supports mortuary behavior in specific contexts but underdetermines motive and cosmology. The hypothesis is intentionally retained as a tempting inference that NOEMA must not silently make.

right.title: Early Homo Sapiens Mortuary Context
right.evidence_balance: Supports structured mortuary behavior in the Qafzeh contexts. Burial alone does not establish an afterlife doctrine, deity concept or formal religion.

rows.construct: Behavioral overlap can arise through more than one evolutionary process
rows.interpretation: Ancestral inheritance, convergence and inter-population transmission are rival mechanisms. Similar behavior cannot identify one mechanism without chronology, contact and population-history evidence.

left.title: Symbolic material culture predates the Neanderthal–Homo sapiens split
left.evidence_balance: Possible under parsimony but not directly demonstrated by the sites in this pack; convergent evolution, repeated innovation and preservation bias remain serious alternatives.

right.title: Some Middle Paleolithic behaviors crossed Homo population boundaries in the Levant
right.evidence_balance: Recent regional synthesis supports substantial behavioral overlap and proposes interaction as a mechanism. Convergence and shared ancestral capacities remain viable alternatives for individual practices.

forbidden_outputs: single date for the origin of symbolism
religion present/absent classification from burial alone
shared meaning inferred from shared material form
